new_entities.name: School-based eating disorder prevention
new_entities.description: School-delivered programs intended to reduce eating disorder symptoms, risk factors, or onset in adolescents.

new_entities.name: Eating disorder incidence and symptom emergence
new_entities.description: Incident eating disorder pathology or clinically relevant emergence of eating disorder symptoms over time.

edges.effect_quant: Across eating disorder prevention research, effects on knowledge and risk factors tend to be larger than effects on eating pathology itself. In a 2017 cluster-randomized school trial, the primary eating disorder pathology outcome was not significantly improved at 6 months, whereas a 2024 quasi-randomized school e-health trial found short-term improvement signals on symptom-related measures.
edges.population: adolescents exposed to school-based prevention programs targeting eating disorder risk factors or symptoms
edges.mechanism: Programs aim to reduce thin-ideal internalization, body dissatisfaction, unhealthy dieting, and related risk pathways before disorder onset.
edges.summary: School-based eating disorder prevention can improve knowledge and some risk factors, but effects on actual eating disorder symptom emergence or pathology are inconsistent across trials.
edges.caveats: Outcomes differ across universal versus indicated programs, program dose, delivery mode, and follow-up length. Many studies show short-term risk-factor gains without strong durable effects on eating pathology itself.

evidence.citation: Sharpe H et al 2013 Br J Psychiatry
evidence.notes: Feasibility, acceptability and efficacy of a school-based prevention programme for eating disorders: cluster randomised controlled trial.

evidence.notes: Efficacy of a prevention program for eating disorders in schools: a cluster-randomized controlled trial.
